cited.quote: Leather Product Park at Panappkkam in Ranipet district and three Food Parks will be
SIPCOT has envisaged to establish a Leather Product Park at the proposed SIPCOT Industrial Park

rationale: C1 is a budget announcement of one Leather Product Park at Panappakkam, Ranipet; C3 says SIPCOT has 'envisaged' it and it is 'proposed'. No GO, tender or sanction appears, and none of the named districts (Dindigul, Vellore, Chennai) is covered. Not started.

cited.quote: The coverage of medical assistance under this scheme has been extended to accident cases

rationale: C2 and C4 concern the New Health Insurance Scheme 2021 for government employees, with accident cases covered generally; C3 covers all road accident victims. None addresses accidents involving government buses specifically, so only related activity is shown.

C1 and C2 describe check dam construction, C3 silt detention in reservoirs, C4 and C5 soil health cards. None mentions allowing farmers to take sediment soil from ponds or check dams free of cost. No extract is about this commitment.

cited.quote: Coordinating with all security agencies such as Coastal Security Group / Indian Coast Guard / Indian Navy

rationale: C1-C5 show coordination with Coast Guard and Navy for search and rescue, a control room, VHF networks, transponders and a mobile app. These are existing or related measures; none is a new measure for live weather feed links with merchant vessels, Navy, Coast Guard and Port Trust.

cited.quote: By the 100th day, following due processes by the concerned departments a total of 2,29,216 petitions were positively disposed

rationale: C2 reports petition disposal by the 100th day, but no extract shows the Chief Minister holding a press conference on the 100th day to brief on actions taken. C1 and C3 concern press releases and publicity, not such a press conference.

cited.quote: additional 2.17 lakh households have been approved to be covered with toilet facilities under Phase II

rationale: C1 reports approval of 2.17 lakh more household toilets under SBM(G) Phase II; C3 reports a Rs.12,000 incentive per household latrine, 3,00,971 latrines built at Rs.335.57 crore and community complexes built from 2021-22 at Rs.70.32 crore. Funds were spent across districts. No dated GO is cited, so the date is given as the year only.

cited.quote: Kalaignarin All Village Integrated Agricultural Development Programme (KAVIADP) is implemented, during the year 2023-24

rationale: C2 reports Village Level Agricultural Development Groups formed in 2,504 panchayats under KAVIADP during 2023-24, with 10,016 trainings for 77,000 farmers. This is a scheme giving training and group support for agriculture and allied activities. The date is only the year written in C2; no GO is cited.

cited.quote: Animal Husbandry sector for allied agricultural activities under Kisan Credit Card Scheme with effect from the year 2021

rationale: C3 says cooperative societies extend 7% loans for animal husbandry (allied) activities under the Kisan Credit Card Scheme from 2021, with interest reimbursed by the Government. This is credit support for allied agriculture, though mainly to individual farmers rather than groups, and the 2021 start is only given as a year.

C1 and C4 concern the real estate regulatory authority and appellate tribunal selection, C2 road safety committees, C3 cooperative structure, C5 local body standing committees. None is a regulatory committee of local government, police, traders and residents' associations for welfare protection.

cited.quote: is launched to provide free emergency medical care during the first 48 hours of an accident
will be extended on a cashless basis on assurance mode under Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance

rationale: C3 says the Innuyir Kappom Thittam - Nammai Kaakkum 48 scheme was launched on 18.12.2021 giving cashless emergency treatment to all road accident victims in the first 48 hours; C4 (GO 46, 2022-02-03) issues its process flow and guidelines. Patients treated are reported in C3.

cited.quote: There was no disinvestment, privatisation or restructuring of PSUs in the State during the year

rationale: C1 and C2 constitute an expert committee on socio-economic statistics, not PSU reform. C3-C5 are audit reports on PSUs; C5 notes no restructuring in its year. No extract shows a committee set up to advise on reforming PSUs.

cited.quote: Increase the Forest and Tree Cover in the State from present 23.8% to 33% by the year 2030-2031

rationale: C4 (GO Ms 126, 2021-12-09) orders the launch of the Green Tamil Nadu Mission with administrative and financial sanction to raise forest and tree cover to 33%; C5 repeats it. C2 also reports the mission as launched. The promise is to undertake steps, which the GO does.

cited.quote: In this context, from the year 2022-23 desilting of
The works includes standardisation of Canals, Channels, Reconstruction / Repair of Irrigation Infrastructures

rationale: Desilting in the Cauvery delta is shown (C1, C2, C4; C5 GO of 2024-02-26), with C4 dating C and D channel desilting from 2022-23. For canals, C3 shows renovation and modernisation of existing canal systems, not new canals; its Grand Anicut sanction predates this government. Desilting is done, new canal building is not shown.

cited.quote: State, and district level advisory committees have been set up to implement the law properly

rationale: C1-C3 describe enforcement of the PC&PNDT Act (decoy operations, prosecutions, advisory committees), the existing arrangement. C4 and C5 set up Special Task Forces for crimes against women and children, a different subject. No special enforcement cell for female foeticide is shown.

cited.quote: Enhancement in ceiling for the supply of Free Electricity to Powerloom Weavers from 751 units to 1000 units
Government have enhanced the free electricity supply to Powerloom weavers from 750 units to 1,000 units

rationale: C1 (G.O. Ms 41, dated 2023-03-03) orders the free electricity ceiling for powerloom weavers raised from 750 to 1000 units bimonthly, and C2 notes the manifesto basis. C3 confirms the enhancement with effect from 03.03.2023 and Rs.374.72 crore released. The promise is met in full.

cited.quote: Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee Recommendations are followed with utmost care for empowerment of minorities

rationale: C1-C3 describe the state's own schemes and its implementation of Sachar recommendations. No extract shows a formal state step urging the Union government to act on the Sachar findings, such as a resolution or letter. State schemes are not advocacy.

cited.quote: A total of 3.95 lakhs SHGs are active in rural and urban areas of Tamil Nadu

rationale: C1-C4 describe existing, mainly women's, SHGs, awards and youth skill festivals and job melas. No extract shows a GO or scheme creating SHGs for unemployed youth. C5 is a monitoring indicator list only.

cited.quote: micro watershed management rain water harvesting structures like farm ponds, field bunds will be formed
towards implementation of Watershed Development Component - Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana

rationale: C2 reports the Chief Minister's Dry land Development Mission, implemented at Rs.146.64 crore in 2021-22 with micro watershed management for dry land farmers. C4 (GO 244, 2022-10-14) sanctions watershed development under the Wasteland Development head in 7 districts. Both parts are covered; the date is only the year written in C2.

cited.quote: TANGEDCO has initiated action to shift meters of Solar power plants from plants to the Substation end

rationale: C1 mentions only moving energy meters of solar plants to the substation end. No extract shows procurement of meters, a tender or a sanction to speed up meter supply for solar generation. C2-C5 are about other renewable or farm topics.

C1-C3 describe weather agro advisories, price forecasts and research projects; C4 dry land research stations; C5 soil health cards. None mentions establishing Agro Clinics for pest and disease study and knowledge dissemination.
